newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CHRISTMAS CHEER FOR HUNGARIAN FANS.
newsitem.headline: CHRISTMAS CHEER FOR HUNGARIAN FANS.

text.p: Hungary's success-starved football fans have received a surprise Christmas present courtesy of the BBC and the English Football Association.

Forty-three years after their football team defeated England 6-3 at Wembley stadium in what has been called "The game of the century," Hungarian fans will at last have a chance to see the whole game on television after the BBC donated a cassette of the full 90 minutes to the cash-strapped Hungarian State Television (MTV).

The game, in November 1953, was the first time that England had been beaten at Wembley and introduced the world to stars such as Ferenc Puskas and Nandor Hidegkuti. Yet, ironically, the Hungarians never saw their greatest moment.
At the time there was no television in Hungary and fans had to rely on radio for information on the action. A few days after the game 20 minute highlights were shown in cinema's across the country.
"The game made Hungarian football famous all over the world and now we will have a chance to see it all for ourselves,"said Jeno Knezy, Head of Sport Department at MTV.
The programme will be shown on Christmas Day and is expected to attract a massive audience.
"The interest is enormous," Knezy said, adding that Hungarian TV would have been unable to purchasee the rights for the game.
The rights were held by the English Football Association whoe waived the rights fee.
"This is a wonderful human gesture, so rare in today's world," he told Reuters.
The idea for the donation came from Britain's Ambassador to Hungary, Christopher Long.
"We wanted to evoke a heroic moment in British-Hungarian sporting history. The fact that it has never been shown before, gives a special resonance here," he said.

Hungarian fans have had little to cheer of late, as their national team have failed to qualify for any major international tournament in over a decade. But the film will recall happy memories fopr many fans such as Robert Szenci, a 74-year old Honved fan.

"I was at college on the day of the game," he said. "The teacher stopped the class and switched on the radio - we all listened to the game together. I will be watching the game, along with 80 percent of my generation."
"It will remind us of the good old days, but the younger fans will be able to see just how good we were," Szenci said.
